name: The Stack Investigates
description: A flat-screen investigative news program produced by a small independent collective operating out of a licensed Tier 2 broadcast slot, covering corponation housing violations, debt collection irregularities, and the Gray Zone infrastructure neglect with a deliberate, unhurried documentary style. The show ran for four seasons before its broadcast license was administratively revoked in 2197 on the grounds of 'failure to maintain editorial balance standards' — a charge the collective disputed in public filings that were themselves never covered by licensed outlets. The episodes remain in circulation on physical media and private mesh shares.
cultural_impact: The show established a generation of Tier 1-2 residents' baseline expectation that genuine journalism would be punished, deepening distrust of all licensed media regardless of editorial intent.
story_hooks: The collective's lead investigator, Saoirse Nakamura-Dube, went underground after the revocation and is believed to be feeding material to pirate outlets under a different name.
A physical copy of the unaired fifth-season pilot — completed before the shutdown — has surfaced at a dead drop, and multiple parties want it.
The licensing authority official who signed the revocation order is now a Tier 4 executive at a Vantablack subsidiary, and someone has connected the dates.
